recipes.name: Slow Cooker Green Beans, Ham and Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds fresh green beans, rinsed and trimmed

steps.text: Halve green beans if they are large; place in a slow cooker with water to barely cover. Add ham hocks and onion. Cover and cook on High until simmering. Reduce heat to Low; cook until beans are crisp but not done, 2 to 3 hours.
Remove ham hocks from the slow cooker. Add potatoes to the slow cooker; cook on Low for 45 minutes.

Meanwhile, remove ham meat from the bones, then chop or shred meat according to your preference. Return meat to the slow cooker after potatoes have cooked. Season with bouillon, garlic powder, onion powder, seasoning salt, and pepper, mixing well.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer green beans, potatoes, and ham into a serving dish with a bit of broth.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Green Beans, Ham and Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: This crockpot green beans and potatoes recipe is made with green beans simmered in a slow cooker with ham hocks, onion, new potatoes, and spices.

video.description: Get ready to impress with the delicious comfort that only a slow cooker can deliver! Add green beans, onion and ham hocks to your crock pot and cook for a few hours, then add new potatoes and cook a while longer, pull out the hocks and shred, then add back with garlic powder, onion powder, seasoning salt, chicken bouillon and black pepper. Serve up beans, potatoes and ham all around with some flavorful broth, and enjoy the “aahs” all around!

review.reviewBody: Yummy! We were pleasantly surprised by how good this was! Didn't have ham hocks, so we used about 2 cups of chopped ham steaks instead. Also, doubled up on the chicken bouillon. We let it cook on low for nearly 10 hours & it was DELICIOUS!! This one's a keeper!

LOVE THIS RECIPE!!!! Will definitely make this again. I did a little subsitution. I used a red onion (in place of a white/yellow onion), smoked sausage (in place of ham) and chicken broth (in place of water). I put everything in the cockpot at one time and cooked on low for 8-10 hrs. It was a hit!!!! I took it to a church potluck and recieved many, many compliments. It is an entire meal!!!

Growing up in eastern PA my mom used to make this after Easter and Christmas when we had ham. I make mine with canned green beans and potatoes, pepper, and a few capfuls of Apple Cider Vinegar and let it come to a boil on the stove and then simmer for 2-3 hours. The Apple Cider Vinegar gives it a nice little kick to it.

My mother made a variation of this when I was growing up, and I've made it for many years myself. However, this is better than she and I made. I could not bring myself to add garlic, and I used ham rather than ham hocks. Put it all in the slow cooker for 12 hours and it was wonderful. It's my new recipe.

I didn't have ham, so I used the turkey sweet Italian sausage that I had and completely compensates by adding real Hormel bacon bits. Also, I cooked stovetop with my Le Creuset. I cooked it covered for around 20 minutes, til the potatoes were cooked, as I had already cooked the sausages in my George Forman grill.

-really you can’t go wrong with green beans, potatoes and ham it’s a great recipe. But due to my taste, I modified it. My modification was as follows. I mix all ingredients together and cook them together instead of using water I used a vegetable stock. I also added a little bit of dill if you don’t want to use a ham hock, I use the ham that comes in the packages already diced they have little bitty dices. They also have larger diced ham, either work great and it’s a fast and easy recipe so there’s no pulling off of the bone finally I cooked the concoction all day in the crockpot on low so this can be prepped the night before and put on in the morning before you go to work and when you come home, you have a great dinner
Its been over 3 hrs nothing is simmering to add potatoes etc. can i cook it on the stove instead.

I love slow cooker recipes and this is one I cook often. I use chicken broth instead of granules and ham steak instead of the hocks. Great easy meal I can pop in the cooker when I get off work in the morning then go to bed. I did half it since we only need 5 servings. And I just throw it in all at the same time.

I grew up with this meal in SW Pennsylania. We use a picnic ham when we make it and we cook it on the stove. We don't put onion in it though, just some basil, salt and pepper. Occasionally, we make dumplings to go into it using my mom's recipe. The recipe for those is very easy. You make the dumplings while the soup is cooking and leave enough time for the dough to dry out a bit on them. After an hour of the soup cooking take off 1 cup of the broth, let it cool. Mix together 2 cups flour; 1/4 tsp of baking soda; 1/4 tsp baking powder. Add the cool broth to the dry mixture, mix well. Roll the dough out with a rolling pin, maybe to a 1/4 inch thick or so, depending how thick you would like them. Let the dough dry a while. Cut into strips about 2 x 2 inch square or more if you would like them larger. (At this point, I will let the dough continue to dry a bit more. About 15 minutes before you are ready to serve the soup, add the squares of dry dough into the soup and gently pat them just below the surface of the broth. The dough is cooked through when they start to float and look like they "puffed up" a bit. They are SO good and it completes this meal. The dumplings, in our household, would replace the bread we would use if we didn't make the dumplings. I hope your family loves these dumplings with ham, bean and potato soup as much as my family!

Good recipe. Fyi, you can use canned beans ( I already had those, so didn't want to go buy fresh). I just cut my potatoes a little smaller, & added everything to the crockpot all at once, cooked on high for two hrs. with bacon as the only meat as I was serving it with pork butt. Also, I season generously with Slap Ya Mama & a salt-free all-purpose seasoning & extra pepper, always!

i love this, my husband not so much. guess thats more for me. I did this on low for about 10 hrs. The meat just fell of the bones. i omitted onions but did a 1tbs of paprika, made some cornbread. i have eaten this for 2 days. Its still delicious! thanks for sharing Sharon

Make this all the time!! Only differences I make, I put 2 12oz bags of frozen green beans in at the start, use a 16oz package or 2 of diced/cubed ham and a 1.5 lb of little potato co potatoes cut up. So easy and delicious for dinner for a couple of days:

I grew up eating this dish, we just called it ham and green beans. My parents were from Pennsylvania so I always thought it is a regional recipe. My mom would make it with leftover ham and canned green beans and salt and pepper for seasoning. Im not a huge fan of it so I seldom made it but my sister loves it and hers tastes just like moms.

Holy cow, was this pretty dang amazing. I used leftover ham i had in the freezer, but everything else was the recipe, modified for 4 servings. True southern food - good, easy and so flavorful 2 of us knocked back nearly the entire slow cooker.
It needed more flavor from spices
I use a leftover holiday ham bone instead of the ham hocks. I make this as a soup in the cold weather months. Using ham base as the broth. So comforting!

This is similar to what restaurants do to make green beans taste better only they usually just use the juice from canned green beans then add chopped onions and chopped cooked bacon. My paternal grandmother taught me this when I was young and said she learned it from her mother who called them “German Beans”. My grandmother used it as a side dish but said big families often stretched it with potatoes to feed a larger family. Either way it’s delicious.
Made as is it’s the Amish recipe for “Beans and specht”. . If possible , Make it like the recipe. My father in law used the butt end where there’s lots of meat and flavor.
We call this "campers special" because it's a one pot meal easy to fix in wilds.
My Husband was skeptical about it until he eat it
